analysis.title: The Pulse of the Market: Higher Ground, Harder Climb - Our Thoughts On the Year-Ahead Outlook For US Equities
key_insights: RBC sets a 12-month S&P 500 target of 8,050, a 16.5% gain from the 11/20/26 close. It was 8,150 in September. The target approximates the output of the revamped valuation/EPS model (fair value 8,063).
The model projects LTM P/E compressing to 18.8x in 4Q27 on $429 trailing EPS (20% growth). Bearish sentiment, solid GDP and strong earnings are expected to offset the compression.

The S&P 500 was down 11.6% from its early October high as of 11/20. That is past Tier 1 (5-10%) but short of Tier 2 (14-20%). RBC says a bottom is not confirmed and an air pocket to 14% is possible, since there have been no 11-12% drawdowns since the GFC.
Precedents for a bottom near 11-12% exist in 1997 (10.8%) and 1999 (12.1%). RBC does not expect the drawdown to go beyond Tier 2 because it sees no EPS contraction, negative GDP or labor breakdown.
Four of the five models are return based and excluded from the target. They signal +15.1% (AAII sentiment), +13.4% (earnings yield gap), +13.7% (Fed test) and +10.2% (GDP test).

Monetary policy and rates are the biggest risk. A 10-year yield above about 6.02% would flip the earnings yield gap model to negative forward returns. Hikes of more than 100 bps in 12 months cut the typical return to 7.4%.
Fed officials' comments about bigger hikes worry RBC more than the Tech wreck. Chunky hiking cycles (1994-95, 2022) left the S&P 500 with more lasting damage than gradual 25 bp cycles.

12-month preference is Value over Growth and Small over Large, though Large Cap Growth may bounce hardest short term. Growth positioning is crowded in Nasdaq futures, Value outperforms when VIX spikes, and political winds are against AI.

Sectors: overweight Financials and Health Care, Tech market weight after the October 14 downgrade, Utilities underweight. Tech valuations have turned attractive but Semis EPS revisions are decelerating.

Small caps are kept on four grounds. Russell 2000 futures are under-owned, forward P/E is below its long-term average, GDP and ISM trends are supportive, and policy is friendlier. Rate-hike pricing is the main headwind.

Valuation and sentiment are not yet at capitulation. The S&P 500 NTM P/E hit 20.5x on 11/5 against a 2022 low of 18.6x, and AAII 4-week net bulls are -11.85% against about -40% at the 2022 and 2025 lows.

Earnings are strong but may be peaking. Consensus has 4Q26 trailing EPS at $356 (+28%) and 4Q27 at $429 (+20%). 2028 operating margins are forecast to dip, driven by Tech and Energy, and Iran war effects on 2027 forecasts are a concern.

Midterm history is mixed. Following-year S&P returns average 16.9% when 3Q or 4Q of the midterm year fell, but only 6.2% when neither did. 4Q26 is down 6.2% as of mid-November. A Republican president with a Democratic Congress averages about 5%.

Retail and positioning signals are fading. Margin debt has stalled below its August peak, Conference Board stock optimism has stalled, and CFTC equity futures positioning has slipped to about 1 standard deviation above average. Bloomberg financial conditions turned slightly negative on 11/20, the first time since April 2025.

AI capex is the key debate. S&P 500 capex growth hit a new high, and investors fear a peak. RBC expects the cycle to be elongated by catch-up outside the top 10, and expects the AI regulation debate to persist through 2027.

earnings_insights: Bottom-up consensus S&P 500 trailing 4Q EPS is $356 for 4Q26 (+28% y/y) and $429 for 4Q27 (+20%). These are consensus estimates, not reported figures.

1Q26, 2Q26 and 3Q26 EPS growth posted sizable positive surprises versus bottom-up consensus. The 3Q26 growth rate is 33.3% for the S&P 500 and 2026 EPS growth is 29.9% as of the latest data, propped up by Tech and Energy.

2027 consensus EPS growth is 20.1% for the S&P 500, ticking down. RBC says this may reflect stale estimates or softening earnings sentiment, and sees Iran war earnings risk lying more in 2027 than 2026.
The share of upward S&P 500 EPS revisions was 64.3% in the latest update, after slipping close to downward-revision territory.

Consensus S&P 500 net income growth is expected to peak in 2026 and decelerate in 2027-28. Tech and Comm Services are forecast at 33% of S&P 500 net income in 1Q28, down from an estimated 48% in 1Q27.
Russell 2000 4Q26 trailing net income growth is 56% (consensus), the same as the AI basket, versus 29% for the S&P 500. For 4Q27 the AI basket is 38%, Small Caps 29% and the S&P 500 20%.
Semis EPS revisions are decelerating, while Software revisions stabilized around 50%.

trade_ideas.description: Favor Small Caps over Large Caps and Value over Growth on a 12-month view
trade_ideas.rationale: Small caps are under-owned with a below-average forward P/E, Growth is crowded, and political winds are against AI.
trade_ideas.risk: More Fed hikes priced in, VIX spikes, and a short-term rebound in Large Cap Growth.

risk_factors: Fed hikes larger or more numerous than expected. Chunky 40-50 bp hikes are historically damaging, as in 1994-95 and 2022.
10-year yield above about 6% would flip the earnings yield gap model negative.
Slower GDP or weaker EPS growth than expected, including AI capex and Iran war effects on 2027-28 estimates.
Further air pocket drawdown to Tier 2 (14-20%, S&P 6,255-6,724) if the market does not stabilize.
AI narrative doubts, capex peak fears, AI and data center regulation, and a Tech EPS revision slowdown.
Cyber and outage events could trigger a Tier 2 drawdown.
Fading retail buying, with stalled margin debt and consumer optimism.
Early 2027 choppiness, with downward revisions to 2027 and 2028 forecasts possible later in the year.
Congressional gridlock, and a less favorable regulatory backdrop for M&A heading into the 2028 election.
charts_described: S&P 500 NTM P/E compression table: 2026 compression from 27.3 to 20.7 (-24.1%) versus a post-1990 major drawdown median of -20.5% on a market-cap weighted basis.
AAII sentiment chart: average 12-month forward S&P return is 15.1% when the 4-week average is between -2 and -1 standard deviations, 14.0% when below -2 standard deviations.
Earnings yield gap chart: -1% to -2% range associated with -3.2% average 12-month forward return, -1% to 0% with 13.4%.
Table of LTM P/E model scenarios: fair values of 7,978 (consensus macro), 8,063 (RBC macro), 7,710 and 7,426 under hike and yield stress scenarios.
Fed hiking cycle table: first-hike drawdowns ranged -8.2% to -14.2% ex-2022 (-25.4%), median -9.6%.
vol_and_positioning: Bloomberg US financial conditions index fell to slightly negative on 11/20, the first time since April 2025 and a bit worse than the Iran war move.
AAII net bulls were -8.90% weekly and -11.85% on the 4-week average as of 11/19. That is between -1 and -2 standard deviations, historically followed by +15.1% 12-month S&P returns.
CFTC asset manager S&P futures positioning has slipped to about 1 standard deviation above average, after not quite reaching +2 standard deviations.
Nasdaq 100 futures positioning still looks over-owned and Russell 2000 futures still look under-owned, with trends narrowing the gap.
Value has outperformed Growth in the 2025-26 VIX spikes, and Growth tends to outperform when VIX eases.
Small caps tend to underperform when VIX spikes or high yield spreads widen, but have held up better than large cap in the recent volatility.
Margin debt stalled slightly below its August peak, suggesting retail buy-the-dip willingness may fade. Household equity allocation hit a new high.
US equity fund flows returned to late 2024 and mid-2026 highs, which RBC reads as a risk of a peak. RBC would not be surprised to see flows take a hit.

S&P 500 bottom-up NTM P/E hit 20.5x on 11/5 against 21.6x and 21.2x at the Iran war and 2025 tariff lows and 18.6x at the 2022 low. The Russell 2000 FY2 P/E is 14.3x against the 11-13x capitulation range.
geopolitical: The Iran war began 2/27/26, and a 9.1% drawdown followed. Voters in the midterms were largely against it (63% said wrong decision), and RBC flags potential Iran war pressure on 2027 earnings forecasts.
The 2026 midterms produced a divided or gridlocked Congress with a less favorable balance of power. AI and data center regulation, affordability and corruption were campaign issues.
State-level AI regulation and anti-data center sentiment are headwinds for the AI trade and the capex cycle.
Tariff and trade policy uncertainty remains elevated, with Liberation Day tariffs (April 2025) cited as a past Tier 2 drawdown.
Betting markets (Kalshi) expect Democrats to keep Congress and retake the White House in 2028, and M&A may pick up ahead of that election.
Cyber and outage concerns are cited as a new tail risk that could turn into a Tier 2 drawdown.

tension_points.bull_case: Bottoms of 10.8% (1997) and 12.1% (1999) are precedents, forward P/Es have returned to recent lows, AAII sentiment is at a contrarian buy level, and no EPS, GDP or labor breakdown is visible.
tension_points.bear_case: No post-GFC drawdown has ended at 11-12%, and an air pocket to 14% is typical. P/E and sentiment have not reached 2022 or 2025 capitulation lows.
tension_points.what_invalidates: EPS contraction, negative GDP or a labor market breakdown, or a rate shock like 2022, would push the drawdown beyond Tier 2.

tension_points.bull_case: Gradual 25 bp hikes see an early drawdown then gains, and hikes of up to 100 bps are associated with +13.7% 12-month returns.
tension_points.bear_case: Chunky hikes averaging about 40-50 bps per move (1994-95, 2022) left the market digging out of a hole, and Fed comments allude to bigger hikes.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Cumulative hikes above 100 bps in 12 months (7.4% typical return), or a 10-year yield above about 6%.

tension_points.bull_case: Growth has more attractive valuations, with R1000 Growth P/E back to average and a better earnings backdrop, and may bounce hardest after stabilization.
tension_points.bear_case: Growth is crowded in Nasdaq futures, loses dominance on earnings sentiment, and political headwinds target AI.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Rising Growth earnings dominance and easing VIX with improving financial conditions would favor Growth.
